Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

maximum noun and adjective and adverb

the most possible; at most

also at most, at the most, at the very most, at the latest, the maximum, as much as possible, top (speed, volume), at the top of one’s voice

classical

Cic. Fam. 2.1.1: bis terve summum
Cic. Att. 13.21.2: hodiē aut summum crās
Traupman 102: hodiē, summum crās, today, at latest tomorrow
Traupman 162
Traupman 212, 213: vīgintī aut summum trīgintā minūtīs, in twenty or at most thirty minutes
Traupman 337

summum

adverb (neuter of summus), after the number or time it limits

at most, at the utmost; at the latest

The everyday way to cap a number: “two or three times at most”; with a time, “at the latest”. Lewis & Short gives it under superus (summus).

Other words

  • quam plūrimum — as much as possible, the most one can

    phrase: quam with the superlative plūrimum, as noun or adverb · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.150: caput autem est … quam plūrimum scrībere; Cic. Rab. Post. 39: ut habēret quam plūrimum (Lewis & Short)

    Quam with any superlative gives “as … as possible”: quam celerrimē, quam maximus (see most).

  • summus, summa, summum — highest, utmost: the maximum (of speed, effort, volume)

    adjective, superlative of superus · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.3.7: summā vōce, at the top of his voice (Lewis & Short); Traupman 110: summā vōce; Traupman 396 · Declension on Wiktionary

    The adjective for a maximum reached: summā vōce, at full volume. See extreme.

Examples

  • ā tē vērō bis terve summum et eās perbrevīs accēpī

    but from you I have had two or three letters at most, and very short onesCic. Fam. 2.1.1

  • exspectābam hodiē aut summum crās ab eō tabellāriōs

    I was expecting couriers from him today, or tomorrow at the latestCic. Att. 13.21.2

  • Caput autem est, quod, ut vērē dīcam, minimē facimus (est enim magnī labōris, quem plērīque fugimus), quam plūrimum scrībere.

    But the main thing, which, to tell the truth, we do least (for it is hard work, which most of us avoid), is to write as much as possible.Cic. de Or. 1.150

  • Fortasse crās, summum perendiē.

    Perhaps tomorrow, at the latest the day after.Traupman 337

  • summā vōce

    at the top of one’s voiceTraupman 396

See also most, least, at least, limit, extreme.
